title: 1957 AHSME Problem 32
statement: The largest of the following integers which divides each of the numbers of the sequence \(1^5-1,\) \(2^5-2,\) \(3^5-3,\) \(\ldots\) \(n^5-n,\) \(\ldots\) is:

solutions.text:
Factor \[ \begin{aligned} n^5-n &=n(n-1)(n+1)\\ &\quad\cdot(n^2+1). \end{aligned} \] Among three consecutive integers, one is divisible by \(3\) and at least one is even, so the expression is divisible by \(6.\) Also \(n^5\equiv n\pmod5\) for every integer \(n,\) so it is divisible by \(5.\) Hence every term is divisible by \(30.\) Taking \(n=2\) gives \(2^5-2=30,\) so no larger listed integer can divide every term.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Show \(n^5-n\) is always divisible by \(2,\) \(3,\) and \(5\)
Use consecutive factors for \(2\) and \(3,\) and residues modulo \(5\) for the remaining factor
